exact_literal_edits.original: For a DM-MAC as in [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac]], a length-$n$ no-feedback code consists of independent uniform private messages $M_j\in[M_j]$, separate deterministic message-only encoders $f_j:[M_j]\to\mathcal X_j^n$, and one joint decoder $g:\mathcal Y^n\to[M_1]\times[M_2]$. The average joint error is $\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne(M_1,M_2)]$; $R_j=n^{-1}\ln M_j$ nats/use. A pair is achievable if a sequence has error tending to zero and limiting lower rates at least the pair; the capacity region is the closure. In particular, independent messages and separate encoders give $X_{1i}\perp X_{2i}$ at every coordinate.
exact_literal_edits.replacement: For a DM-MAC as in [[def-it-two-user-discrete-memoryless-mac]], fix integers $n\ge1$ and $M_1,M_2\ge1$, and write $[m]=\{1,\ldots,m\}$. A length-$n$ no-feedback code consists of independent uniform private messages $\mathsf M_j\in[M_j]$, separate deterministic message-only encoders $f_j:[M_j]\to\mathcal X_j^n$, and one joint decoder $g:\mathcal Y^n\to[M_1]\times[M_2]$. The average joint error is $\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne(\mathsf M_1,\mathsf M_2)]$; $R_j=n^{-1}\ln M_j$ nats/use. A pair is achievable if a sequence with $n\to\infty$ has error tending to zero and limiting lower rates at least the pair; the capacity region is the closure. In particular, independent messages and separate encoders give $X_{1i}\perp X_{2i}$ at every coordinate $1\le i\le n$.

Because $n\ge1$ and $M_j\ge1$, each rate $n^{-1}\ln M_j$ is a finite nonnegative real number.
